statement: Let P be the set of prime integers p satisfying left <= p <= right. The function returns a result r such that len(r) = 2, and: (a) if |P| < 2, then r[0] = -1 and r[1] = -1; (b) if |P| >= 2, then, writing a = r[0] and b = r[1], (i) a and b are prime, (ii) left <= a < b <= right, (iii) for every pair of primes x,y with left <= x < y <= right, b - a <= y - x, and (iv) for every pair of primes x,y with left <= x < y <= right and y - x = b - a, a <= x.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 2.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000.

statement: Let P be the set of prime integers p satisfying left <= p <= right. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = [-1, -1] if and only if |P| < 2.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2 and r != [-1, -1], both r[0] and r[1] are prime integers.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2 and r != [-1, -1], both r[0] and r[1] lie in the inclusive interval [left, right].
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2 and r != [-1, -1], r[0] < r[1].
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2 and r != [-1, -1], for every pair of prime integers x,y with left <= x < y <= right, r[1] - r[0] <= y - x.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2 and r != [-1, -1], for every pair of prime integers x,y with left <= x < y <= right and y - x = r[1] - r[0], we have r[0] <= x.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2 and r != [-1, -1], there is no prime integer p satisfying left <= p <= right and r[0] < p < r[1].
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

statement: For any second pair left', right' of 64-bit integers also satisfying 1 <= left' <= right' <= 1000000, if the set of prime integers p with left <= p <= right equals the set of prime integers p with left' <= p <= right', then whenever the function returns r on (left,right) and r' on (left',right'), we have r = r'.
preconditions: left and right are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= left <= right <= 1000000. An integer n is prime iff n >= 2 and its only positive divisors are 1 and n.
